title: Abraham and the Three Strangers
text:
Abraham was sitting at the entrance of his tent by the oaks of Mamre in the heat of the day when he looked up and saw three men standing nearby. He did not wait for them to approach. He ran from the tent to meet them, bowed to the ground and begged them not to pass by. "Let a little water be brought so you can wash your feet and rest under the tree," he said, "and I will fetch a bite of bread so you can refresh yourselves."

The bite of bread turned into a feast. Abraham hurried into the tent and told Sarah to quickly knead fine flour and bake cakes. He ran to the herd himself, chose a tender calf and gave it to a servant to prepare. Then he set curds, milk and the meat before his guests and stood near them under the tree while they ate.

"Where is your wife Sarah?" they asked. "In the tent." Then one of them said, "I will surely return to you about this time next year, and Sarah your wife will have a son." Sarah, listening at the tent door, laughed to herself, because she and Abraham were very old. The visitor asked why she had laughed, and whether anything was too hard for the Lord.

The guests, Genesis makes clear, were messengers of God. A year later Sarah gave birth to Isaac.
lesson: Welcome people warmly and generously before you know who they are or what they can do for you. Hospitality reveals character.
place: Oaks of Mamre (Ramat al-Khalil), near Hebron, West Bank
